content.title: Chelsea Football Club selects IFS as Principal Partner
content.description: Chelsea Football Club today announces a multi-year global partnership with IFS, the world's leading provider of Industrial AI. As part of this commitment, IFS will be elevated to Principal Partner with immediate effect, featuring on our front of shirt for the remainder of the 2025/26 season — marking the beginning of a long-term collaboration that places advanced AI at the heart of football performance, operational excellence and fan engagement.

content.title: Saturday football is back at Villa Park
content.description: Fixtures Aston Villa Vs. Leeds United - Sat, Feb 21st 2026, 15:00 A sold-out Villa Park awaits this Saturday as Aston Villa welcome Leeds United for a 3pm kick-off in B6. Supporters are encouraged to arrive early, welcome the team on Trinity Road, and make the most of the pre-match atmosphere for our first Saturday 3pm game for over a year. The Warehouse will be open before and after the game, with food, entertainment and activities for fans to enjoy throughout the day and a detailed schedule of what’s on can be found below. Every match matters, and your support this weekend will be crucial once again. If you missed out this weekend, limited tickets remain available for our next home fixture against Chelsea on Wednesday, 4 March. More details can be found here. Warehouse auditorium launch Supporters will be welcomed into the Warehouse auditorium at Villa Park on Saturday, with a whole host of pre-match and post-match activity at the all-new facility planned. In an exciting step towards the full opening of the new Warehouse matchday fanzone later this season, supporters will be able to access the main Warehouse auditorium, in addition to the Food Court and external Plaza areas for the very first time. Here's your entertainment guide for Saturday... 12pm – Doors open and pre-match entertainment commences 12.30pm – Live sport on the screens: West Brom v Coventry City (Championship) 1.15pm – James Chester and Rachel Daly Q&A on stage with Alan McInally 1.40pm – Band (Quadrox) on stage and live sport on the screens: West Brom v Coventry City (Championship) and England v Ireland (Six Nations) 2.45pm – Warehouse closes for kick-off 3pm – Kick-off 4.30pm – Warehouse reopens and post-match entertainment commences 5.10pm – VillaTV live stream on the screens: Post-match show 5.30pm – Band (Big Classics) on stage and live sport on the screens: West Ham v Bournemouth (Premier League) and Wales v Scotland (Six Nations) 8pm – DJ on stage and live sport on the screens: Manchester City v Newcastle United (Premier League)

content.title: Pundits predict who will win the Premier League title
content.description: Six picks for Arsenal and five for Man City. See who our pundits are backing to lift the 2025/26 Trophy
content.body:
Eleven Premier League pundits have given us their latest predictions for who will win the 2025/26 Premier League title, with nearly HALF of them backing Manchester City over Arsenal. 

Man City are now only five points behind leaders Arsenal, who have dropped points in each of their last two matches, at Brentford and Wolverhampton Wanderers, and face a trip to Tottenham Hotspur in the north London derby on Sunday. 

With Man City also having a match in hand over Arsenal, and the two teams going head-to-head in a massive head-to-head at the Etihad Stadium in April, we are in a remarkable position whereby the title race is in both teams' hands.

But WHO will lift the Premier League Trophy come May? We asked that exact question to a selection of pundits.

You can see their answers below, and we want to hear your thoughts. Vote below.

The execution result shows exactly the broadcast schedule data (pageInfo + content array of events with broadcasters/channels) that the user task requires for a given date range.

data_quality.reasoning: The js_evaluate step parses document.body.innerText as JSON and returns the full object without truncation or reshaping. The sample execution shows rich, structured data including pagination, event IDs, names, startDateTime, broadcasters, channels, and nested contentReference objects, matching the exploration summary for this endpoint.

parameter_coverage.reasoning: All meaningful query parameters for this endpoint (from, to, page, pageSize) are exposed as routine parameters with appropriate types and descriptions. A minor nit is that page and pageSize are marked required even though they have sensible defaults; they could be non-required with defaults instead, but this does not break functionality.

routine_robustness.reasoning: The routine uses a simple navigate to a public GET endpoint with no auth or token dependencies, aligning with exploration that these APIs are unauthenticated. It includes basic error handling in js_evaluate (returns ok:false with error message on parse failure). Slight robustness concerns: relying on document.body.innerText assumes the response is rendered as text; using response interception or contentType checks would be more resilient, but current approach worked in execution.

structural_correctness.reasoning: Operations are in a valid order: navigate -> js_evaluate that writes to session storage -> return that reads from the same key. The session_storage_key is consistently used, and there are no missing dependencies or misuse of placeholders. No auth or prior navigation is required for this API, so a single direct navigate is structurally appropriate.

recommendations: Consider making page and pageSize parameters optional with defaults instead of required, to simplify typical usage when callers just want the first page with a standard size.

If available in the platform, prefer accessing the raw response body (e.g., via a fetch-style operation or responseText) instead of document.body.innerText, which could be brittle if the environment wraps JSON in additional markup or error pages.

Its parameterization aligns well with the endpoint's capabilities, and the operation sequence is structurally sound and robust enough for public, unauthenticated use.
